entries.title: How do I search the menu to find a page quickly?
entries.answer: Use the Search the menu box at the top of the left sidebar. Type part of a page name, what it does or its category, for example templates, phones or audit. Press Enter to open the top result, use the arrow keys to pick another, or press Escape to clear it. You can also ask AVA where something is and she will open it for you.

entries.title: How long does initial data sync take?
entries.answer: First-time syncs typically complete within 5–15 minutes depending on lead volume. You can monitor progress in the Sync Health dashboard.

entries.title: Can I import leads from a CSV file?
entries.answer: Yes. Go to Lead Management → Bulk Actions → CSV Upload. The system maps columns automatically and flags duplicates before import.

entries.title: What is the difference between an Agent and a Manager role?
entries.answer: Agents see only their assigned leads. Managers see all leads across their portfolio and can reassign, bulk-act, and view team analytics.

entries.title: How do I clock in and track breaks?
entries.answer: Click "Clock In" in the top-bar widget next to your profile menu, or go to /time-clock. A live timer starts immediately. Use Start Break/End Break to pause the visible timer without ending your shift, and Clock Out when you finish. Your worked time always excludes break time.

entries.title: Can I see who is currently clocked in?
entries.answer: Admins and owners see a "Team Status" tab on the Time Clock page listing everyone currently clocked in or on break, with a live running timer and an idle indicator for each person.

entries.title: What happens if I forget to take a break or step away?
entries.answer: After 8 minutes of no mouse/keyboard/touch activity while clocked in, you get an on-screen "Are you still working?" prompt. If there's no response within 2 more minutes, the system automatically starts a break so idle time never counts as worked hours. Coming back and using the app again automatically resumes your timer. If you stay away for 45+ minutes total, the system automatically clocks you out.

entries.title: How do I resurface warm leads before agents call?
entries.answer: Use the ML Prospect Scoring page. The "Warm Leads" panel automatically surfaces high-engagement prospects with a blended score above your threshold.

entries.title: Can I assign leads to multiple agents?
entries.answer: Yes. The bulk reassign workflow supports assigning to a single agent or moving to a territory, which then distributes based on your assignment rules.

entries.title: What does the regulation badge mean?
entries.answer: The regulation badge shows the STR compliance status for the property's city/state. Green = compliant, Yellow = restricted, Red = prohibited.

entries.title: What is the STOP rate and why does it matter?
entries.answer: The STOP rate is the percentage of SMS recipients who replied STOP to opt out. A rate above 2% signals your messaging may feel spammy — review template tone and frequency.

entries.title: How do escalation triggers work?
entries.answer: When a lead replies or clicks a link, the system automatically escalates them out of the automated sequence and flags them for agent follow-up in the Escalated Leads view.

entries.title: Can I A/B test templates?
entries.answer: Yes. Create two template variants and assign them to separate sequences. Compare engagement rates in the Template Performance dashboard.

entries.title: How do I share a report with a homeowner?
entries.answer: Use Scheduled Exports in Advanced Reports. Add the homeowner's email as a recipient and set the frequency. They receive a formatted PDF without needing portal access.

entries.title: What is the Executive Overview vs Analytics?
entries.answer: Executive Overview shows high-level KPIs for leadership. Analytics provides granular breakdowns by source, stage, agent, and time period for operational decisions.

entries.title: Why are some leads showing as "stale"?
entries.answer: Leads are marked stale when their enrichment data is older than your configured freshness threshold (default: 30 days). Re-enrich them from the Lead Data Quality page.

entries.title: How do I reconnect a disconnected integration?
entries.answer: Go to Integration Hub, find the disconnected service, and click "Re-authenticate". This restarts the OAuth flow without losing your existing configuration.

entries.title: Can homeowners see agent contact details?
entries.answer: No. The homeowner portal is scoped to portfolio-level metrics only. Agent names, emails, and internal notes are never exposed.

entries.title: How do I export the compliance audit log?
entries.answer: Go to Compliance Audit → Export. You can filter by date range, agent, and action type before downloading as CSV or PDF.

entries.title: Dashboard — Your Command Center
entries.answer: The Dashboard gives you a real-time snapshot of your entire STR lead pipeline. KPI cards surface total leads, active pipeline, high-priority prospects, and your personal commission payout — all scoped to your selected portfolio. Key features: KPI cards: total leads, active pipeline, action-needed count, your commission payout; Stage Funnel Chart showing conversion across pipeline stages; Top Leads Table with prospect scores and regulation status; Activity Feed for recent team actions and system events; Portfolio switcher to scope all data to a specific market. Tip: Pin your most-used portfolio in the sidebar switcher to load it by default every session.

entries.title: AVA — Your Assistant on Every Screen
entries.answer: AVA is the assistant in the bottom-right corner of every screen: look for the round electric-blue AVA button (it pulses in the corner now). If you ever tuck her away, tap the blue AVA tab on the right edge to bring her back. Ask her how anything works, where a page is in the menu, or for your leads, follow-ups and counts, and she answers from the approved help and your live data. She can open pages, point at things and walk you through any menu category. You can type, tap the microphone, say "Hey AVA", or turn on spoken replies and talk with her. Key features: Ask how any screen works, or "where is…?", and AVA opens the page for you; Say "walk me through the Outreach menu" for a guided tour, item by item; Search leads, check follow-ups, get a daily briefing and see lead counts by stage, source or state; Find her in the bottom-right corner of every screen, and tap her any time you need help; AVA asks for your approval before she creates a follow-up or changes a lead, and only reports it done once it is saved; Search the menu with the box at the top of the left sidebar to find any page quickly. Tip: Start with "What can you do?" or "Walk me through the menu". AVA only sees what your role allows, and she never clicks or types for you.

entries.title: Data Sync & Quality — Keep Lead Data Current
entries.answer: Admins control the data engine that feeds every outreach workflow. Use Data Sync, Source Intelligence, duplicate detection, freshness checks, and enrichment review queues to keep lead records accurate before agents call or message homeowners. Key features: Run and monitor lead-source sync jobs across configured markets; Review import quality, duplicate detection, and address mismatch reports; Track data freshness so agents are not working stale listings; Use enrichment review queues before accepting owner/contact updates; Watch system health and retry queues for failed sync or provider events. Tip: Data quality is upstream of every call and campaign. Fix duplicate, stale, or mismatched leads before assigning them to agents.

entries.title: Lead & Homeowner Pipeline — Work Your Prospects
entries.answer: Lead Management is where you spend most of your time. Browse, filter, enrich, and act on every lead. Leads tagged "Inbound — Self-Qualified" are warm homeowners who opted in via the AVYRO AI estimate page — prioritize these above cold sync-sourced leads. Key features: "Inbound — Self-Qualified" tag = homeowner opted in via estimate landing page (warm lead); Full-text search across names, addresses, notes, and tags; Saved filter presets for instant recall of common views; Bulk SMS dispatch and sequence assignment; Inline enrichment panel: owner lookup (Stage 1) and contact enrichment (Stage 2). Tip: Filter by "Inbound — Self-Qualified" first — these leads already expressed interest and convert at a higher rate than cold outreach.

entries.title: Map View — Check Market Coverage and Pin Accuracy
entries.answer: Map View shows where your non-synthetic leads are located across active markets. Use it to spot market concentration, verify that pins match the lead city/state, and select properties before drilling into the full lead record. Key features: Shows all available map-ready leads, not only the first 1,000; Filters by regulation status, minimum score, and bedroom count; Pin color reflects STR regulation status for quick market scanning; Lead list and detail panel stay synced with the selected map pin; Use map clustering patterns to guide assignment and outreach strategy. Tip: If a pin looks wrong, check the lead address, city, state, zip, and coordinate fields before assigning that lead for outreach.

entries.title: Dialer & Teleprompter — Your Highest-Frequency Daily Action
entries.answer: The Teleprompter is your live call companion. It auto-fills lead details into your script, surfaces objection responses in real time, and logs every call to the Activity Timeline automatically — no manual entry needed. Key features: One-tap call start from any lead record; script auto-fills with lead name, address, and property details; Live objection library: pre-built responses surface before falling back to AI generation; Call disposition capture: outcome logged and lead stage updated automatically on hang-up; Every call auto-logged to Activity Timeline (duration, outcome, timestamp, recording link); Post-call summary generated and saved without manual entry; Call recording consent disclosure and state-specific guidance appear before live transcription starts. Tip: Use the "warm inbound" script variant for "Inbound — Self-Qualified" leads — it opens by acknowledging they reached out, not re-introducing AVYRO AI from scratch.

entries.title: Messaging Tools — SMS, Email & Follow-Up Sequencing
entries.answer: SMS and email templates share the same merge-field resolution system as the Teleprompter — one unified system, not three separate implementations. Follow-up sequences extend the cadence engine with SMS and call as additional channel options per stage. Key features: SMS and email templates with merge-field autofill (same system as Teleprompter); Follow-up sequencing: add SMS/call steps to any cadence stage; A2P 10DLC brand/campaign registration required before SMS goes live (hard blocker); Pre-send compliance checklist: DNC check, time-of-day restrictions, TCPA consent; Template performance tracking: open rates, click rates, reply rates per template. Tip: Check A2P 10DLC registration status in Settings before sending any SMS — unregistered numbers will be blocked by carriers.

entries.title: Scheduling & Calendar — Manage Follow-Ups
entries.answer: The follow-up sequencing engine handles automated cadence scheduling across email, SMS, and call steps. Leads auto-advance through stages based on call outcomes — interested leads move to follow-up, no-answers queue for retry. Key features: Auto-trigger cadences when leads hit stage thresholds (interested → follow-up, no-answer → retry); Scheduled queue panel showing upcoming touchpoints per lead; Manual override: reschedule or skip any step from the lead record; Cadence performance metrics: completion rate, escalation rate, per-step engagement; Calendar view of all scheduled outreach across your lead portfolio. Tip: Sort cadence performance by escalation rate descending to find your highest-converting sequences and clone their structure.

entries.title: Documents & E-Signature — DocuSign from a Lead Record
entries.answer: Trigger the DocuSign Partnership Agreement flow directly from any lead record. Once the homeowner signs, the system auto-logs the completion, updates the lead stage, and triggers your commission calculation. Key features: Send Partnership Agreement via DocuSign from the lead's detail view — one click; Signing status tracked in real time: sent → viewed → signed → completed; DocuSign completion = commission trigger (system-verifiable event); Embedded signing portal: homeowner can sign without leaving the AVYRO AI flow; Void and resend available if the homeowner needs a corrected document. Tip: After sending a DocuSign, check the Activity Timeline on the lead record — signing events are logged there in real time so you know exactly when the homeowner opens and signs.

entries.title: Hiring & Offer Letters — Recruit and Onboard the Team
entries.answer: Admins can manage candidate profiles, interview scripts, scorecards, pipeline stages, offer letters, and DocuSign signing for new hires. Interview Mode is admin-only and should be used to standardize candidate evaluation. Key features: Candidate Profiles store parsed resumes, strengths, concerns, and scorecards; Interview Mode gives admins structured interview scripts and role-play prompts; Candidate Pipeline tracks ready, interviewed, follow-up, move-forward, hired, and rejected stages; Moving a candidate to Hired opens a branded offer-letter draft; Offer letters can route through DocuSign once credentials are configured. Tip: Keep Interview Mode restricted to admins so hiring notes, scorecards, and candidate data stay separated from agent outreach tools.

entries.title: Performance & Reporting — Your KPIs & Commission Status
entries.answer: Your personal performance dashboard shows only your own numbers — leads worked, calls made, conversion rates, and commission payout. Portfolio-wide revenue figures are not shown here; you see only what's owed to you. Key features: Commission payout card: pending payout, next scheduled payout date and amount; Total commission earned: current period and lifetime (toggleable); Payout via Stripe Connect on the schedule defined in your commission agreement; Commission triggered by DocuSign completion of the Partnership Agreement; Call analytics: your personal volume, conversion rate, and outcome breakdown. Tip: Commission calculations are tied to DocuSign completion — if a payout looks wrong, check the lead's Activity Timeline to confirm the signing event was captured.

entries.title: Team Admin — Roles, Assignments, and Agent Readiness
entries.answer: Admin tools control who can access what, which leads agents receive, and whether agents are ready to work. New agents should complete their mandatory orientation before they start calling leads. Key features: Invite agents and monitor whether their onboarding tour is complete; Assign high-priority or fully verified leads to the right agent queue; Use role management to keep admin-only pages away from agents and homeowners; Review agent workload, performance, productivity, and coaching views; Use audit logs and compliance reports to trace sensitive changes. Tip: Before assigning call volume, confirm the agent is active, has completed onboarding, and has verified leads with phone numbers in their queue.

entries.title: Time Clock — Shift Tracking for Every Team Member
entries.answer: Every admin and agent can clock in/out and track breaks from the top bar or the Time Clock page. A live timer runs continuously while clocked in and pauses visually during breaks — no separate timesheet tool needed. Key features: Clock In / Start Break / End Break / Clock Out from the top-bar widget on every page; Live HH:MM:SS timer visible at all times once clocked in; Personal 14-day shift history and this-week total on the Time Clock page; Admins/owners get a "Team Status" tab showing everyone currently clocked in or on break in real time; Only one open shift per person is allowed at a time — clock out before starting a new one. Tip: Use the Team Status tab to spot agents who forgot to clock out — a stuck shift keeps accumulating hours until it is closed.

entries.title: Q&A / Help Center — Your Ongoing Support Resource
entries.answer: The Help Center is your go-to after this tour. Ask questions about your own leads, stats, and how any module works — the AI assistant answers from your actual dashboard data and AVYRO AI's internal documentation, not from guesses. Key features: AI assistant answers from your dashboard data and AVYRO AI's how-to documentation; Ask about your own leads, stats, commission status, or any module's features; Compliance or legal questions route to a human admin — AI will not guess on those; Search AVYRO AI's internal documentation for step-by-step module guides; This is your primary support resource after completing this tour. Tip: After this tour, the Help Center is your first stop for any question. The AI assistant has context about your specific leads and stats — ask it directly rather than searching generic docs.

entries.title: Ask AVA: how AVYRO works
entries.answer: At every step, AVA is there. She is the assistant built into each screen: she answers how-to questions, opens the page you need, walks you through the menu, finds leads and follow-ups, and can speak and listen. When something should change she asks you first, and only reports it done once it really is. Includes: Answers from your help center and your team's own notes; Opens pages, points at them and runs guided tours; Available to admins, owners and agents, within their role.

entries.title: What are Seller & owner services?
entries.answer: When a homeowner's reply suggests they may sell, it lands in Seller & owner services as an opportunity for a person to review. Nothing is sent automatically: each step needs the owner's recorded permission, and a person approves which service fits. The screen has seven tabs: Dashboard, Opportunities, Campaign, Partners, Referrals, States and Revenue. AVYRO only flags the reply for your team; it never contacts the owner on its own.

entries.title: How does a lead become a seller opportunity?
entries.answer: AVYRO reads a homeowner's text reply for signs they might sell, such as saying they want to sell, are thinking about selling, want to put the property on the market, or ask for an offer or what it is worth. A clear statement counts as explicit; a mention of selling counts as possible; a reply that says they are not selling is not flagged. The reply is flagged for a person only, so nobody is contacted automatically. You can also flag a lead as a seller manually on the Opportunities tab: paste the lead's link or id and add a note, for example after a phone call. The Dashboard can also scan past replies for sellers; it shows how many it found and asks you to confirm before adding them, and nothing is sent to them.

entries.title: What are the stages of a seller opportunity?
entries.answer: An opportunity moves through seven stages, in order: Seller signal, Permission and verification, Qualified, Routed to a service, Human consultation, Agreement, and Outcome. It can only move forward when the requirements for the next stage are met, and the screen lists what is still missing.

entries.title: What do I need before an opportunity can be Qualified?
entries.answer: To move an opportunity to Qualified you need to: confirm the person is the owner or an authorized decision-maker; record the owner's timeline; record whether the property is occupied, vacant or rented; record whether the owner decides alone; and record the owner's permission for a consultation. If anything is missing, the opportunity stays where it is and the screen shows what to add.

entries.title: Why does seller work need the owner's permission?
entries.answer: Each step needs the owner's recorded permission for that specific purpose: estimate follow-up, sale consultation, long-term management, short-term rental management, readiness services, or sharing details with a partner. Permissions are kept in an append-only record, so a withdrawal is added as a new entry and the history is never overwritten. An opt-out or STOP reply withdraws every purpose at once, and an opportunity with no valid permission is blocked until a person records it again.

entries.title: Which services can an owner be routed to?
entries.answer: An owner can be routed to one of five services: a licensed sale partner, long-term management, short-term rental management, interim rental before sale, or property readiness services. Each needs its own permission from the owner (sharing details with a partner for a sale, long-term management, short-term rental management for both short-term and interim rental, or readiness services). A person must also review and approve that the owner is eligible for the service before the opportunity can be routed.

entries.title: What does a sale partner need before I can route an owner to them?
entries.answer: Before an owner is routed to a licensed sale partner, choose the partner on the opportunity, and the partner must have a verified license, have had their arrangement reviewed legally, and have the signed partner agreement on file. You manage partners in the Partners tab.

entries.title: What is needed to reach the Agreement stage?
entries.answer: An opportunity can only move to the Agreement stage once an agreement has been added to it. Add invoices and costs from each opportunity; the Revenue tab then shows what was invoiced, collected and spent for each service, and the margin (collected revenue minus the cost of delivering the service).

entries.title: Who can see Seller & owner services?
entries.answer: Seller & owner services is for admins and owners. It only shows your own organization's opportunities.

entries.title: How do I teach AVA a new answer?
entries.answer: Admins and owners can open AVA Knowledge from the menu. It lists the help topics AVA could not answer (words only, counted for people who chose to share anonymous usage) and the topics people rated not helpful. Pick a topic or start from a blank form, type the question and the answer, and publish it: AVA uses a published answer right away, for your organization only. You can save a draft, edit an answer, unpublish it or remove it at any time. Keep answers to facts and leave out passwords or private details, because everyone on your team can ask AVA for them.

entries.title: What can AVA do?
entries.answer: I'm AVA, the assistant built into AVYRO. I can explain how any screen works, tell you where a page is in the menu and open it for you, walk you through a whole menu category one item at a time, or run a guided tour of a screen. I can search your leads, show details and why a lead scores the way it does, list follow-ups and leads still to verify, give you a daily briefing, and count leads by stage, source, state, contact status, skip-trace result or sale versus rent. With your confirmation I can create a follow-up, move a lead to another stage or mark a follow-up done, and offer an export of what is on screen. I point and open, but I never click or type for you, and I only change something after you approve it. Admins and owners see everything in their organization; agents see their own leads.

entries.title: How do I hear AVA and talk to her out loud?
entries.answer: Open AVA and turn on Spoken replies at the bottom of her panel; she then reads her answers aloud in a natural voice, and you can pick a different voice from the Voice list. Turn on Talk with me and, after she speaks, she listens for your reply, so you can have a back-and-forth without typing. Tap the microphone to speak a question at any time, or say "Hey AVA" once the microphone is allowed. If you say nothing she stops listening. Speaking to her needs Chrome, Edge or Safari and microphone permission; if her natural voice is ever unavailable she uses your browser's voice instead. Captions can stay on while she talks.

entries.title: Can AVA show me around the menu and explain every page?
entries.answer: Yes. Ask me to walk you through any menu category, for example "walk me through the Outreach menu", and I'll move from item to item in the sidebar, pointing at each one and explaining what it is for. Ask "where is Cron Job Monitor?" and I'll tell you which menu it is in and open it for you. Long menus are split into short tours of ten items, so you can stop whenever you like.

entries.title: Can AVA tell me how many leads I have?
entries.answer: Yes. Ask for counts by pipeline stage, listing source, state, contact status (verified, with a phone number), skip-trace result, or for sale versus for rent. Admins and owners get totals for the whole organization; agents get counts for their own leads. The numbers come straight from the lead database when you ask, and I'll say when they were taken.

entries.title: Who is AVA, what is she like, and what is her favorite color?
entries.answer: I'm AVA, the AVYRO assistant. I'm an AI, not a person, but I do have a personality: upbeat, warm and a little playful, and always happy to help. My favorite color is electric blue, which is why I glow that color, my favorite page is the Pipeline Board because I love watching leads move across it, and my favorite moment is when a team gets unstuck.

entries.title: Where do I find AVA, and how do I bring her back if I hide her?
entries.answer: AVA is the round electric-blue button in the bottom-right corner of every screen for admins, owners and agents. Tap it to open her. If you tucked her away with Hide, tap the blue AVA tab on the right edge of the screen to bring her back, or say "Hey AVA" once your microphone is allowed. You can drag her to a different spot, and Focus mode keeps her out of the way until you need her.

entries.title: How do I find and track broker partners who accept referrals?
entries.answer: Use the Partners tab in Seller & owner services. Add each broker or team lead with their role, brokerage, niche, license number and state, whether they accept referrals, whether they will report outcomes, their typical referral fee and how they like to send updates. Move them through To contact, Emailed, Call booked, Partner or Pass. Each partner shows a link to the state's official license lookup and the date you last checked the license; a check older than 90 days is marked for another look. A partner meets the pass criteria when they accept referrals, agree to report outcomes and have a verified license. The Recruiting playbook at the top has the first email and the five qualifying questions. Admins and owners only.

entries.title: How do I record what a partner broker reports back on a lead?
entries.answer: Use the Referrals tab. Record each lead you send to a partner, then log each status they report with the date it applied: received, contacted the owner, listed (MLS number optional), under contract, then closed (close price optional) or dead (one-line reason). A lead can only be sent when the partner's license is verified, legal review is done, the agreement is on file, the partner is licensed in the property's state, that state is switched on in the States tab with counsel's sign-off, the partner has not stopped reporting, and the owner's permission to share their details is recorded. Statuses only move forward, and closed or dead ends the referral. Admins and owners only.

entries.title: How do I know if a partner broker has stopped reporting?
entries.answer: Each partner card on the Partners tab shows an update rate: of the referrals sent more than a week ago, how many have any status beyond sent. The target is 70%. A partner is marked Watch when one referral has not been acknowledged after a week, one open referral has had no update for a month, or the rate is under 70%. They are marked Not reporting when the rate is under 70% across at least three referrals, or two or more referrals are unacknowledged or a month without an update. Use the Needs attention filter to see them, and consider pausing a partner until they catch up.

entries.title: How do I clear a new state before sending leads to a partner broker there?
entries.answer: Use the States tab in Seller & owner services. It lists all 50 states and DC, each with its regulator. Activate states one at a time, in the order seller-intent leads appear. For each state, check the regulator's own site and answer four questions: can a licensed broker pay and receive a referral fee, can an unlicensed person be paid (almost always no), must the fee go through the brokerage, and is a written referral agreement required. Record the statutes you checked, the official license lookup, and the counsel who reviewed it with the date. A state can only be switched to Pilot or Live once counsel's review date is recorded, and leads in a state that is not switched on cannot be sent to a partner. You can download the whole tracker as a spreadsheet. The researched notes for Arizona, Nevada and Colorado are pre-filled for counsel to confirm. This is a checklist, not legal advice.

entries.title: What are the general rules for real estate referral fees between brokers?
entries.answer: Across essentially every state, referral fees between licensed real estate brokers are allowed, while paying an unlicensed person for a real estate referral is prohibited or heavily restricted. The fee normally goes brokerage to brokerage rather than agent to agent, the payee must hold an active license, and a written referral agreement before the introduction is best practice (Colorado treats a contractual referral relationship as part of reasonable cause). States do not generally cap the percentage; 20 to 35 percent is custom, not law. What varies by state is who may be paid (out-of-state brokers, inactive licenses), the payment path, whether the agreement must be written, and any required disclosures, which is why each state is cleared in the States tab with counsel before the first paid referral. This is general information, not legal advice.

entries.title: Can NAVEO take a fee for referring escrow or title companies, or act as an escrow company?
entries.answer: No. Escrow, title and mortgage are settlement services. Under RESPA Section 8, giving or accepting a fee, kickback or other thing of value for referring that business on a federally related mortgage loan is prohibited, as are unearned fee splits. NAVEO Homes refers owners to licensed real estate brokers only. It does not accept or pay per-closing fees for sending escrow, title or mortgage business, and it does not hold earnest money or closing funds, which needs an escrow license and bond from the state regulator (for example Arizona's Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions or Nevada's Mortgage Lending Division). The owner chooses their own escrow or title company. If NAVEO ever owned part of such a company, a compliant affiliated business arrangement with the written Appendix D disclosure, no required use, and payment only as a return on ownership would be needed, with RESPA counsel. Decline any offer of money per closing until counsel has reviewed it. This is general information, not legal advice.

entries.title: How does the NAVEO Homes broker referral model work, and who does the licensed work?
entries.answer: NAVEO Homes sources and qualifies permissioned seller leads and refers them to a licensed real estate broker under the National Real Estate Referral Partner Agreement, one form for all 50 states and DC, signed before the introduction. Each partner's commercial terms (fee percentage, protection period, days to pay, exclusivity, responsible broker) are recorded from its Exhibit A on the Partners tab. The national form does not replace state clearance: each state is still checked and signed off in the States tab, and some states need extra forms or disclosures for out-of-state referrals. The partner broker performs all licensed brokerage activity and holds an active license in the property's state; NAVEO does not act as the listing broker or broker of record. The fee is a percentage of the commission the partner actually receives on a closed referred transaction, paid to NAVEO by the brokerage on the terms in the agreement's Exhibit A, and no fee is owed if the deal does not close unless the exhibit says so. The partner reports status as set out in Exhibit B: received, contacted, listed, under contract, closed or dead, with a first update within seven days. NAVEO can suspend new leads if the partner's license is not active or reporting stops. Management through NAVEO Stays is optional for the owner and never a condition of the sale referral. This is a summary, not legal advice.

entries.title: How are referral fees calculated and tracked when a partner closes a deal?
entries.answer: On the Referrals tab, when a partner reports a lead closed you record the commission they received and the date. The fee is the agreed percentage of that commission, to the cent, and it is due the agreed number of business days after the partner was paid (weekends skipped). The percentage, protection period, payee, payment method and due days are copied onto each referral when it is sent, so renegotiating later never changes an old deal. You then mark the fee invoiced and, when it arrives, paid with the amount; a short payment is flagged, and a fee past its due date shows as overdue. The Referral fees summary shows what is owed now, what is overdue, what has been paid, and how many closes are still waiting on a commission, with a labelled rough estimate from the close price. If a referral was marked dead but the same owner lists or closes with the partner inside the protection period, you can reopen it and the fee is still owed. A lead cannot be sent until the partner's fee percentage, protection period, payment method and payee are on record. Bank account numbers should not be stored in AVYRO; keep wire and ACH details in a secure vault.

entries.title: Can AVYRO check a broker's license against the state's records?
entries.answer: For Arizona and Colorado, yes. On a partner with a license state and number, press Check against state records. AVYRO reads the state's published records (Colorado's open data and Arizona's public database download), confirms the license is active, and also checks that the name or brokerage on the record matches the partner, so a wrong number is not accepted. It shows the license type, expiry, employing brokerage and any discipline listed, and warns when it is a salesperson license because the fee must go through the employing broker. Verified partners are re-checked every week; if the state shows a license as inactive it is marked expired and new referrals to that partner stop. Other states, Nevada included, do not publish records in a form AVYRO can read, so someone still checks the official lookup and records the date. Brokerage (entity) licenses in Arizona also have to be checked on the state site.

entries.title: How does AVYRO pick the best broker partner for a lead?
entries.answer: On a lead's profile (admins and owners) the Partner broker panel, and on the Referrals tab, choose a lead whose owner has given permission and AVYRO suggests the best partners. A partner is only suggested if it is active, license verified, agreement and legal review done, licensed in the lead's state, not marked do not assign, not at its maximum open leads, not flagged as having stopped reporting, and covers the lead's market, property type and budget band where those are known. The rest are shown with the reason each was ruled out. The suggestions are ranked: a city match counts most, then a county match, a budget in the middle of their band, a good update rate, earlier closes, an exclusive territory and any manual boost. If no partner qualifies, the lead is shown as needing a partner, so recruit one for that state; the owner can still be offered the NAVEO Stays path meanwhile. The state must also be switched on in the States tab before a lead can be sent.

entries.title: How do I email a partner broker about a lead, ask for a status or send the fee details?
entries.answer: Once a lead has been sent to a partner (on the lead's Partner broker panel or the Referrals tab) there are three emails, each sent only when you press its button. Email lead packet sends the partner a lead reference, the property, the owner's name and phone as permitted, the agreed fee and protection period, and how to report. It is refused if the owner's permission to share is no longer recorded or the lead is marked do not contact. Ask for a status update asks the partner for a one-line status, and can only go out once every three days. Email fee details is available when the referral is closed: it reminds the partner of the fee, the payee and the days to pay, and asks for the commission received and its date. Partners reply with the lead reference in the subject, for example Lead AZ-2026-A1B2C3, Contacted. Replies go to your own email, and you record the status on the referral. Every email is logged with its status so you can see what was sent and whether it failed. Text messages to partners are not sent from AVYRO.

entries.title: What is the seller and owner outreach campaign?
entries.answer: The campaign helps your team find out what an owner actually wants for a property, then send them one clear next step: sale, long-term rental (NAVEO Homes), short-term rental (NAVEO Stays), or both and still deciding. It starts with one short text and email asking which they want, then follows with a message matched to their answer. The goals are to separate real seller intent from curiosity or rental interest, route to the right service, confirm permission and purpose instead of assuming it, give each owner one authorized next step, and never promise a sale, a valuation or any regulated activity in a message. A STOP reply withdraws every permission at once. Every text and email names the NAVEO that matches the property: NAVEO Stays for a home for rent and NAVEO Homes for a home for sale. TRAVLR is no longer used in messages to owners.

entries.title: What is the first message to send an owner, and how do they answer?
entries.answer: The entry text says who you are, mentions the property address, and asks one question: are you mainly looking to sell, rent long-term, rent short-term, or still deciding? The owner replies 1, 2, 3 or 4. The email asks the same question with the same four options, as a reply or a button. Suggested email subject lines to test: Quick question about the address; Sell, rent, or both? We need 10 seconds; So we don't send the wrong options. Only the path they choose is followed up. If the property is for sale, don't ask the four-option question. The Campaign tab has a 'for sale' choice: the first message is from NAVEO Homes, says NAVEO connects owners with a licensed local broker to guide the sale, and, if the home will sit empty while it's listed, that NAVEO Stays may be able to run it as a short-term rental in the meantime. It ends with one simple ask. It never mentions property management and never promises a price, timeline or income.

entries.title: Where does each reply (1, 2, 3 or 4) go?
entries.answer: Reply 1 (sale) goes to seller solutions, with a qualification call and an authority check. Reply 2 (long-term rent) goes to NAVEO Homes, with an eligibility and scope call. Reply 3 (short-term rent) goes to NAVEO Stays, with a short-term rental checklist and fit review. Reply 4 (both or still deciding) goes to an options consultation and an options map call. If there is no reply after two touches, the owner is held for gentle nurture with soft re-engagement only.

entries.title: What do I send an owner who wants to sell?
entries.answer: Tell them what happens next in three steps: confirm they have authority to discuss the property; capture their timeline, whether it is occupied, and their goals; then route them to the correct licensed pathway or service options. Say plainly that this is not a listing appointment and that you will make no promises about price or sale until the proper steps are complete. Ask them to reply YES for a short qualification call, or to give a preferred timeline such as 30 days, 90 days or exploring.

entries.title: What do I send an owner who wants long-term rental management?
entries.answer: Confirm what they chose, then describe what NAVEO Homes focuses on: tenant placement and screening, ongoing property oversight, clear owner reporting, and local compliance and vendor coordination. The next step is a short qualification to confirm eligibility and scope, with no commitment needed to have the conversation. Ask them to reply YES for a short call or to send preferred days.

entries.title: What do I send an owner who wants a short-term or vacation rental?
entries.answer: NAVEO Stays handles setup and operations where the property and local rules allow it. Before anything else, check local short-term rental rules and building restrictions, insurance and safety requirements, the owner's goals and timeline, and whether the property is a realistic operational fit. If it clears those gates you can discuss management scope and onboarding. Ask the owner to reply YES to receive the short eligibility questions or a quick call.

entries.title: What do I send an owner who is open to more than one option?
entries.answer: Keep it practical: confirm their current situation (occupancy, timeline and goals), show which paths are realistically available among sale, long-term rent and short-term rent, and give one clear recommended next step with no pressure. Ask them to reply YES for a short options conversation.

entries.title: What if the owner does not reply to the first message?
entries.answer: Send a soft follow-up, not a push. On day 3, a short text circles back about the property, says you are happy to help whether they lean sale, rent or still deciding, and repeats the 1, 2, 3, 4 options. On day 7, an email says there is no rush and that you are keeping the door open, repeats the four options, and says you will only send the matching next step. After two touches with no reply, hold the owner for nurture and do only soft re-engagement.

entries.title: What are the rules for the seller and owner campaign?
entries.answer: Never award or route an owner automatically based on score alone. Confirm consent and purpose before deeper outreach. Scores help you prioritize work; they do not authorize any activity. Each property record gets one clearly authorized next step. Make no automatic promises of a sale, a valuation or any regulated activity.

entries.title: How should I label owners in this campaign?
entries.answer: The playbook recommends labelling every lead with five things: primary intent (sale, long-term rent, short-term rent, both, or unknown); service fit (Homes, Stays, seller solutions, or review); authorization status (contact OK, purpose confirmed, opted out, or needs reconfirming); timeline (0-30 days, 30-90 days, 90+ days, or exploring); and occupancy (vacant, owner-occupied, tenanted, or unknown). These are recommended labels for tracking the campaign; AVYRO's seller screen today records intent and fit scores, authorization status, timeline and occupancy on each opportunity.

entries.title: How should I test the campaign first?
entries.answer: Run a 14-day test. Take 30 to 50 existing authorized leads, send the entry text and email, tag every reply with one of the four intents, and run the matching branch campaign. Measure the reply rate, the share that choose a clear path, the share that book a qualification or options call, and any opt-outs or complaints.

entries.title: Where do I find the campaign messages in AVYRO?
entries.answer: Open Seller & owner services and choose the Campaign tab. It lists the first text and email, the text and email for each of the four answers, and the day 3 and day 7 follow-ups. Choose whether the property is for rent or for sale, then type the owner's first name, your name and the address, and every message fills itself in. Messages for a home for rent come from NAVEO Stays and messages for a home for sale come from NAVEO Homes; use Copy to copy a message or its subject line, then send it yourself from your own text or email. Copying sends nothing. When an owner has answered, their opportunity also shows the matching messages.

entries.title: What does AVYRO do when an owner replies 1, 2, 3 or 4?
entries.answer: AVYRO records the answer on the owner's seller opportunity (it creates one if they have none), shows what they chose in the Opportunities list, sets the next step for your team, and alerts the admins. It only counts as an answer when the last text you sent that owner was the campaign question, the one containing the line "Reply with 1, 2, 3 or 4", and when the whole reply is just the answer, such as 2 or Option 2. A longer reply is left for a person to read. Nothing is sent back to the owner automatically, and the answer does not choose a route, grant permission or approve eligibility: your team confirms who they are and records their permission first. A STOP reply withdraws every permission.

entries.title: What is NAVEO Homes?
entries.answer: NAVEO Homes is the long-term rental management service an owner can be routed to. It focuses on tenant placement and screening, ongoing property oversight, clear owner reporting, and local compliance and vendor coordination. The first step is a short qualification call to confirm eligibility and scope, with no commitment needed to have the conversation.

entries.title: What is NAVEO Stays?
entries.answer: NAVEO Stays is the specialist short-term and vacation rental operation for eligible properties. It handles setup and operations where the property and local rules allow. Before anything else the team checks local short-term rental rules and building restrictions, insurance and safety requirements, the owner's goals and timeline, and whether the property is a realistic operational fit. If it clears those checks, management scope and onboarding can be discussed.

entries.title: What is NAVEO seller solutions?
entries.answer: Seller solutions is where an owner who wants to sell goes. It is not a listing appointment, and no promise about price or sale is made until the proper steps are complete. The team first confirms the owner has authority to discuss the property, captures their timeline, occupancy and goals, and then routes them to the correct licensed pathway or other service options if the timing is not right.

entries.answer: Texts, emails and messages to the owner of a home that is for sale are sent as NAVEO Homes, with one main offer: an introduction to a licensed local broker who guides the sale. NAVEO does not list or sell homes itself; in each state a state-licensed broker partner handles the sale. They then say that, if the home will sit empty while it's listed, NAVEO Stays may be able to run it as a short-term rental in the meantime, and end with one simple ask such as 'Worth a short conversation?'. They never say NAVEO sells or lists the home itself, never mention property management, and never promise a sale price, a timeline or income. A home for rent is sent as NAVEO Stays instead.

entries.title: What is in the Core menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Core menu for admins and owners has 10 pages: Dashboard (Your command center: KPI cards for the lead pipeline, the stage funnel, top-scored leads and the recent activity feed); Executive Overview (How outreach is converting across the company, with cards, bars and rows you can click to dig into the detail); Pipeline Board (The campaign board: one column per stage, one card per lead with its score and latest activity, plus filters by state, program, minimum score and sort order); Map View (Leads plotted on a map so you can see where properties are and open one from its pin); Field View (Mobile) (A phone-friendly view for working leads in the field: touch a pin to see the lead, with call-quality feedback and assignment override); Time Clock (Clock in and out and track your breaks); Team Chat (Message your team inside AVYRO); My Profile & Prefs (Your own profile and preferences); System Health (Live status checks of every AVYRO service, with a 90-day history you can click into by day); AVA Knowledge (Teach AVA answers for your team and see what she could not answer).

entries.title: What is in the Leads & Pipeline menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Leads & Pipeline menu for admins and owners has 14 pages: Lead Management (Search, filter and work every lead); Lead Record (Full record, notes and activity); Lead Profile (Owner, property and contact details); Lead Sources (Where leads come from and how they convert); Lead Sources Manager (Add, pause and tune lead sources); ML Prospect Scoring (Model-driven prospect scores); Property Screening (Qualify properties before outreach); Property Report (Revenue estimate and market report); Questionnaires (Owner intake and qualification forms); Duplicate Detection (Find and merge duplicate leads); Duplicate Audit (Review past merges and matches); Dedup Monitor (Live duplicate detection health); Renewal Alerts (Upcoming agreement renewals); Agreement Signing (Send and track agreements).

entries.title: What is in the Property Operations menu for admins and owners?

entries.title: What is in the Data & Sync menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Data & Sync menu for admins and owners has 19 pages: Data Sync (Run and monitor data imports); Sync Health (Sync status and failures); Trulia Source Integrity (Checks that the Trulia lead source is still delivering clean data, with a button to run a sync for that source); Data Freshness Monitor (How current each data source is); Sync Ops Dashboard (Live source pulls, per-portfolio health, validation and alerts for the data sync); Sync Regression Monitor (Flags synced leads that fail quality checks, so a source that starts returning bad data is noticed within days); Sync Diagnostics (Row-by-row detail of sync runs: click any row to expand what happened and why); Enrichment Rules Engine (The saved confidence rules for enrichment, and any real violations caught during validation); Validation Analytics (How enrichment results hold up under validation: pass and fail rates over time); Contact Enrichment (Find phones and emails for owners); Enrichment Review Queue (Enrichment results that need a person to approve or reject them before they are trusted); Source Intelligence (Share, quality, verification and conversion per lead source, computed from real counts of the leads); Enrichment Costs (What enrichment and skip-trace lookups cost, so you can keep spending in check); Integration Health (Whether each connected service (sync sources, messaging, email) is up and responding); CSV Pre-Flight (Validate a CSV before import); Re-Score Events (An audit log of every lead score change: who triggered it, when, old versus new score and the reason); Lead Data Quality (Where lead records are missing or inconsistent, so they can be fixed before outreach); Data Quality Monitor (Ongoing data-quality checks across the lead database and how they trend); Verification Debug (Trace any property through the verification pipeline to see why it did or did not pass).

entries.title: What is in the Outreach menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Outreach menu for admins and owners has 28 pages: Email Templates (Branded outreach emails); Auth Email Templates (Sign-in and invite emails); Message Templates (Reusable SMS and email messages); Template Editor (Create and edit templates); Template Ratings (Which templates agents rate best); Template AI Suggestions (AI rewrites to lift replies); Cadence Engine (Build multi-step outreach cadences); Cadence Performance (Reply and conversion by cadence); Cadence AI Insights (AI tips to improve cadences); Escalated Leads (Leads needing a human follow-up); Follow-Up Sequences (Automated follow-up steps); SMS Delivery (Delivery status for every text); Campaigns (Plan and launch campaigns); Co-Host Pipeline (Co-host prospects and offers); Seller & Owner Services (Seller replies, permissions and partners); SMS Campaign Analytics (Texting results by campaign); Inbound Threads (Replies from homeowners); Bulk Outreach Composer (Send to many leads at once); Bulk Email Outreach (Bulk email with tracking); Email Campaigns (Email campaign builder); SMS Cadence Templates (Text templates for cadences); Delivery KPIs (Delivery, bounce and opt-out rates); Outreach History (Every message sent to a lead); Outreach Tracking (Opens, clicks and replies); Retry Queue (Failed sends waiting to retry); Alert Hub (System and outreach alerts); Alerts Inbox (Your unread alerts); Info-Request Links (Homeowner info-request links).

entries.title: What is in the Calls menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Calls menu for admins and owners has 21 pages: Live Teleprompter (The call workspace: a live script and lead details for making calls); Interview Mode (The live teleprompter in interview mode, used when interviewing candidates); Live Lead Queue (The live queue of leads waiting for an agent); Interview Calendar (Scheduled candidate interviews on a calendar); Interview Recordings (Recordings of past interviews to review); Candidate Profiles (Hiring candidates and their profiles in one place); Candidate Kanban (Hiring candidates on a board, moved between stages); Candidate Pipeline (The hiring funnel: how many candidates sit at each stage of recruiting); Resume vs. Interview (Compares what a candidate said in their resume with what they said in the interview); Interview QA (Question-and-answer review for interview mode); Candidate Tracker (A tracker for every candidate and where they stand); Offer Letters (Create and track offer letters for candidates); Candidate Sequences (Automated messages sent to candidates as they move through hiring); Hiring Analytics (Recruiting metrics: how candidates move through hiring and where they drop off); Headset Setup (Set up and test your headset and microphone for calls); Call Analytics (Call volume, outcomes and talk time across the team); Cron Job Monitor (Whether the scheduled background jobs (syncs, enrichment, sends) are running on time and what they did); Agent Coaching (Coaching for agents); Call Quality Review (Review the quality of calls); Lead Auto-Assign (AI lead auto-assignment: how new leads are given to agents); AI Score Retraining (Record closed-deal outcomes so the prospect scoring model can be retrained, and see past retraining runs).

entries.title: What is in the Analytics & Reports menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Analytics & Reports menu for admins and owners has 21 pages: Analytics (Overall lead and outreach analytics); Advanced Reports (Deeper reports you can slice by market, source, agent and period); Campaign Analytics (Results per campaign: sends, replies and conversions); Template Performance (Which message templates get replies and which do not); Outreach Performance (How outreach performs by channel, agent and message); Activity Timeline (A timeline of recent activity); Audit Trail (A record of who changed what in the system); Admin Audit Log (The administrator-level log of sensitive actions); Compliance Audit (Checks outreach against compliance rules such as opt-outs and quiet hours); Compliance Change Log (A history of changes to compliance settings and rules); City Regulations / STR (Short-term-rental regulations by city, so you know the rules before you pitch an owner); Trace Regulation (Trace a city regulation record); Pre-Launch Checklist (The pre-launch compliance checklist for a property: click an item to cycle its status and open its reference); Onboarding Doc Review (Review and approve the documents homeowners upload during short-term-rental onboarding); Checklist Automation (Settings that automatically advance stale onboarding checklist steps and remind homeowners about pending items); CRM Export (HubSpot) (Send leads to HubSpot); Scheduled Exports (Exports that run on a schedule and are delivered to you); CSV Export (Download leads as a CSV file with the columns you choose); AI Score Breakdown (Why a lead has its score: how much each factor contributed); ROI Calculator (Work out revenue against cost and the return on outreach and enrichment); Lead Lifecycle Funnel (The funnel from new lead to live property, with the drop-off at each step).

entries.title: What is in the Agents & Team menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Agents & Team menu for admins and owners has 18 pages: Agent Management (Add, edit and set up agents, including territories and lead permissions); Workspace Management (Manage workspaces); User Management (Manage user accounts, roles and whether each person is active); Agents (Legacy) (The earlier agents screen, where you change an agent's role, territories and default lead permissions); Agent Leaderboard (Agents ranked by activity and results); Agent Performance (Per-agent performance: calls, conversions and trends); Conversion Analytics (How each agent's leads convert, stage to stage); Close Rate Analytics (Close rates across the team, by stage and source); Agent Routing (Band) (Agent routing: a lead batch report and weekly actual versus predicted conversion); Agent Productivity (How much each agent gets done: calls, texts and follow-ups); Team Performance (Team-wide performance at a glance); Team Agent Performance (Per-agent call volume, conversion rates, talk time and coaching flags, with a 7-day view); Team Lead Board (Every lead on the team's board, with the option to reassign a lead); Agent Workload Board (How many leads each agent is carrying, so work can be balanced); Manager Team Metrics (Manager view of the team: stage breakdown by agent and revenue against cost with ROI); Agent Onboarding (Onboarding for a new agent); Bulk Agent Invite (Invite many agents at once); Commission Rules (Set how agent commissions are calculated).

entries.title: What is in the Tools & Admin menu for admins and owners?
entries.answer: The Tools & Admin menu for admins and owners has 25 pages: AI Features (The AI features of the app (Claude), shown with whether the API key is configured to switch them on); Workflows (Build email and SMS sequences that automate outreach); Operations (Property operations: cleanings, maintenance and inventory across all properties); Integration Hub (Connect services, manage API keys and watch usage quotas); Subscription & Billing (Your subscription and billing); Admin Management (Admin tools for SMS templates (variables fill in at send time) and pre-built replies to common homeowner objections); Admin Config (API keys, verification status, rate limits, sync intervals and environment settings); Webhook Inspector (See the webhooks AVYRO has received and what they contained, to debug an integration); Base44 Submissions (Submissions received from the Base44 forms); Ops Monitoring (A real-time operations dashboard: API health, delivery rates, enrichment syncs, webhook health and an incident timeline); Performance Dashboard (Real-time latency, render, API and session health); Performance Diagnostics (Performance diagnostics for the app); Score Simulator (Try changes to the scoring and see how leads would score before you apply them); Scoring Rules (The rules behind the prospect score); Score Weight Editor (Adjust how much each factor counts toward the prospect score); Bulk Actions (Apply one action, such as an assignment or stage change, to many leads at once); Roles & Permissions (Roles and permissions: who can see and do what); Event Dashboard (A dashboard of system events as they happen); Nurture Cadence (The nurture cadence engine: choose a sequence and manage the long, gentle follow-up for leads who have not replied); Notification Prefs (Choose which notifications you receive and how); Homeowner Notifications (Notifications sent to homeowners); Session Management (Signed-in sessions); Team Onboarding (Onboarding for the team); Agent Profile (Your agent profile); Help Center (Answers, articles and guides for every part of the app).

entries.title: How is the menu organized for admins and owners?
entries.answer: Admins and owners see 9 menu categories on the left: Core (10), Leads & Pipeline (14), Property Operations (2), Data & Sync (19), Outreach (28), Calls (21), Analytics & Reports (21), Agents & Team (18), Tools & Admin (25). Each category opens to show its pages. I can open any page for you and point at it in the menu, or walk you through a whole category.

entries.title: What is in the Core menu for agents?
entries.answer: The Core menu for agents has 5 pages: My Dashboard (Your own dashboard: today's work, your leads and what needs doing next); My Leads (The leads assigned to you, to search, filter and work); Time Clock (Clock in and out and track your breaks); Team Chat (Message your team inside AVYRO); Follow-Ups (Your leads that have a follow-up due).

entries.title: What is in the Calls menu for agents?
entries.answer: The Calls menu for agents has 3 pages: Call Workspace (The call workspace: a live script and lead details for making calls); Headset Setup (Set up and test your headset and microphone for calls); Call History (Every message sent to a lead).

entries.title: What is in the My Performance menu for agents?
entries.answer: The My Performance menu for agents has 3 pages: My Performance (Your own results: calls, conversions and goals); My Activity (A timeline of recent activity); My Commissions (Your own commissions and what they are based on).

entries.title: What is in the Help menu for agents?
entries.answer: The Help menu for agents has 3 pages: Help Center (Answers, articles and guides for every part of the app); My Profile (Your own profile and preferences); Account Settings (Your account settings and preferences).

entries.title: How is the menu organized for agents?
entries.answer: Agents see 4 menu categories on the left: Core (5), Calls (3), My Performance (3), Help (3). Each category opens to show its pages. I can open any page for you and point at it in the menu, or walk you through a whole category.
